## Cleanup must compare ownership before deleting a slot keyed by a shared id (P1)

Pattern: a cleanup handler for a failed or superseded job deletes a record keyed by a shared resource id (for example `store.active.pop(workspace_id)`), when it should only delete the record if the job still owns it (for example `association["setup_id"] == setup_id`).

Why it is dangerous: a queued or retried cleanup that runs after a newer job has completed silently wipes the newer job's state. This happens even when operations are fully serialized, so it is not a concurrency bug.

Signals:
- the change is described as a "simplification" that removes an ownership guard;
- an owner field that is written (for example `setup_id`) is no longer read anywhere.

Fix: compare-and-delete. Read the slot, check the owner id, and delete only on a match. Add a regression test for this order: older job fails, newer job completes, then the older job's cleanup runs.

Seen in: workspace setup cleanup review (cleanup.py, 2026-10-11).
